title: Expectation, then surprise (However / Nonetheless / That said / Actually)
subtitle: Transitions · 29 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **29 of the official questions in Transitions are this one** — 9 Easy, 12 Medium, 8 Hard.
Most versions sit at the Medium tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- Sentence one sets up a belief, assumption, appearance or hope: 'may seem', 'many assume', 'have long believed', or a list of big achievements.
- The blank sentence reports the reality that undercuts it, such as a failure, a correction or an unexpected exception.
- Choices include one concession or correction word and several continuation words.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Ask whether sentence two is what sentence one would lead you to expect.
- 2) If it isn't, you need a concession: however, nonetheless, that said, still.
- If sentence one is a mistaken belief and sentence two gives the true fact, 'actually' or 'in fact' fits best.
- 3) Check that the choice doesn't also claim a cause, which would be wrong here.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: First, you pick 'for this reason' or 'moreover' because both sentences are about the same topic and you never check the direction of the logic.
Second, you rule out 'however' when sentence one is a string of successes, because you don't notice that sentence two ranks one success above all the others and so pivots against the list.

sections.heading: You are losing these
